facts.statement: Akanthosuchus is an extinct genus of alligatoroid crocodilians known as the "spine crocodile" due to its dermal armor.
facts.quote: Akanthosuchus ("spine crocodile", referring to its dermal armor) is an extinct genus of alligatoroid crocodilian

facts.statement: The genus Akanthosuchus was described by F. Michael O'Neill and colleagues in 1981.
facts.quote: F. Michael O'Neill et al. described the genus in 1981

facts.statement: The type species A. langstoni was named in honor of paleontologist Wann Langston Jr.
facts.quote: The type species is A. langstoni, honoring paleontologist Wann Langston Jr.

facts.statement: Later research confirmed Akanthosuchus langstoni existed in the older Puercan-age portion of the Nacimiento Formation.
facts.quote: Later work identified Akanthosuchus langstoni from the older Puercan-age portion of the Nacimiento Formation as well

facts.statement: The time range for Akanthosuchus is the Danian to Selandian stages, from 66 to 60.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Selandian (66 to 60.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Akanthosuchus are found in the Paleocene-aged Nacimiento Formation of the San Juan Basin in New Mexico, United States.
facts.quote: Fossils are known from the Paleocene-aged Nacimiento Formation of the San Juan Basin in New Mexico, United States

facts.statement: The spikes on the armor rose up to 29.0 mm, nearly as tall as the base of the scutes they sat on.
facts.quote: The spikes were nearly as tall as the base of their scutes were long, rising up to 29.0 mm

facts.statement: The thigh bone of the type specimen was 137 mm long, while the shin bone was 102 mm long.
facts.quote: The thigh bone of NMMNH NP-139 was 137 mm long, and the shin was 102 mm long

facts.statement: Analysis of growth rings suggests the type specimen was at least eight years old when it died.
facts.quote: Based on growth rings, Hill and Lucas suggest that it was no younger than eight years old when it died

facts.statement: The tail may have been relatively short, indicated by the reduction of bony projections on the tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The tail may have been relatively short, given the reduction of bony projections on known tail vertebrae

facts.statement: O'Neill and colleagues suggested Akanthosuchus was an alligatorine based on characteristics of a partial lower jaw bone.
facts.quote: O'Neill et al. suggested that Akanthosuchus was an alligatorine, based on the characteristics of a partial lower jaw bone (retroarticular)

facts.statement: Hill and Lucas later used cladistic analysis to reject the idea that Akanthosuchus is the same as Ceratosuchus or Navajosuchus, finding it to be an alligatoroid.
facts.quote: More recently, Hill and Lucas, using a cladistic analysis, rejected the hypothesis that Akanthosuchus is the same as either Ceratosuchus or Navajosuchus, and found that Akanthosuchus is an alligatoroid

facts.statement: Akanthosuchus belongs to the parent group Alligatoroidea.
It is debated whether Akanthosuchus is strongly an alligatorine, as Hill and Lucas found this classification to be weakly supported.
facts.quote: Hill and Lucas found that this was weakly supported in their analysis

facts.statement: Akanthosuchus is unique among known crocodilians for possessing both spiked and bladed scutes.
facts.quote: Spiked and bladed scutes are not unknown among crocodilians, although no other known crocodilian had or has both

facts.statement: The armor of Akanthosuchus was unusual for having elongate spikes or broad blades.
facts.quote: The armor was unusual in having elongate spikes or broad blades
